title: Death, the Scales, and Regret in the Fire

paragraphs.text: The Prophet is told to push back evil with what is best. Allah knows well what they say. He should seek refuge in Allah from the whispers of the devils, and from their coming near him.

When death comes to a disbeliever, he says, "My Lord, send me back, so that I may do good in what I left." But these are only words. Behind them is a barrier until the Day they are raised. When the Horn is blown, family ties will not matter, and no one will ask about another. Those whose scales are heavy with good deeds will succeed. Those whose scales are light have lost themselves and will stay in Hell forever. The Fire will burn their faces.

They will be asked, "Were My verses not recited to you, and you denied them?" They will say their misery overcame them and they went astray. They will beg to be taken out and promise not to return to evil. Allah will say, "Stay there in shame, and do not speak to Me." Some of His servants used to pray for forgiveness and mercy. But the disbelievers mocked them and laughed at them, until they forgot to remember Allah. Today Allah has rewarded those servants for their patience, and they are the winners. Then Allah will ask how many years they stayed on earth.
